introduction: Follow seven exact key assemblies through the wyrm chambers, then return Tiamat cadaver proof for a two-item tribute. Shared access, death drops and vault services have distinct outcomes.
orientation: Meet the oddly-clothed man in the Meditation Room. Ask key, fragment, item, something, for, me or tiamat. He can assemble seven different keys from exact fragment sets, and fashion two tribute items from the exact bits and pieces of Tiamat. His replies are addressed questions echoed to the room, not automatic quest completions for listeners.

The huge golems at the outer gate block ordinary eastward passage while present. Worshipers at the Pool of Worlds can carry the dark key. The ordinary key route then leads through the bright, ruby-encrusted, golden and jeweled keys, followed by bronze, red and green. This explains access; supplied keys or shared open doors can bypass earlier exchanges without fabricating your own crafting history.

Collect the bright-key pair from the black and blue wyrms in the northeast chamber. The ruby-key triple belongs to the three green wyrms in the northern chamber. Keep all three ruby fragments distinct even though they have the same visible name.

The blue and red wyrms in the southeast chamber carry the golden-key pair. The southern red wyrm and two following white wyrms carry the jeweled-key triple. These are exact material types, not a requirement to kill any three creatures with a matching color.

At the lair entrance, the shadow dragon and brilliant white wyrm carry the bronze pair. The northern side chamber carries the white, black and green wyrm fragments for the red key. The southern side chamber carries three other exact fragments for the green key. Repeated mobile prototypes in different rooms do not make their fragments interchangeable.

Most assembled keys and the translucent crystal key can break after successful unlocking. Dark-key stock has a different break value. Unlocking, opening, finding a secret door and actual arrival are separate outcomes. A crafted receipt remains after its key is used or spent.

Tiamat is a distinct imported boss prototype. Her native stock can include the exact cadaver bits at a thirty-three-percent roll, and the immaterial spirit at a separate ten-percent roll. Her death releases carried and equipped stock onto the floor and has a separate timed-heart creation path. The heart, spirit, poison stinger and ordinary corpse do not replace the craftsman cadaver offering.

The cadaver exchange grants both the polished scale and strip of flesh through one accepted history. It does not require you personally to have killed Tiamat, looted her first, drunk from the pool or touched the monolith. Supplied exact proof can prepare the native exchange.

Ask the pitiful slave torment, beg or end for his plea. His death procedure selects one of four rare item types. This is a separate native death outcome without a craftsman recipe or an authored rescue achievement. Hearing his plea, finding a rare item or receiving a kit copy does not prove your own rescue or recovery.

The Wisdom pool and epic monolith before the vault have separate services. The pool has a level requirement, a shared pool cooldown tag and a possible stat change. Epic touching uses its own committed authority. Neither service is an invented prerequisite for the eight exchanges.

Some load, wandering and potion rooms are outside the ordinary player entrance graph. The missing throne-procedure destination and an inactive-file potion reference require builder review. These are not hidden exploration requirements or promised new rewards.

Reset mode zero does not automatically replenish these fragments, the boss or rare services. The current catalog keeps eight achievements and eight potential dailies; potential does not guarantee fresh supply. Active accounting refuses fresh reset item issuance, and legacy death creation needs its own owned integration before additional story credit.

Carry each exact offering loose. Nested or equipped proof, same-name substitutes, keys from another branch and reward copies do not complete an accepted exchange. Current preparation remains separate from historical acceptance. All new story credit requires active, ready accounting.
